questions.question: The income of three playback singers Aswath, Sunita and Ramdin are in the ratio of 12 ∶ 9 ∶ 7 and their expenditures are in the ratio 15 ∶ 9 ∶ 8. If Aswath saves 25% of his income, what is the ratio of the savings of Aswath, Sunita and Ramdin?
questions.questionHtml: The income of three playback singers Aswath, Sunita and Ramdin are in the ratio of 12 ∶ 9 ∶ 7 and their expenditures are in the ratio 15 ∶ 9 ∶ 8. If Aswath saves 25% of his income, what is the ratio of the savings of Aswath, Sunita and Ramdin?
questions.solution:
Income → Aswath : Sunita : Ramdin → 12x : 9x : 7x

Expenditures → Aswath : Sunita : Ramdin → 15y : 9y : 8y

Savings = Income - Expenditures

Aswath : Sunita : Ramdin → 12x - 15y : 9x - 9y : 7x - 8y

Given:

Aswath saves 25% of his income for future investments

12x - 15y = 25% of 12x

=> 12x - 15y = 3x

=> 9x = 15y

=> x / y = 15 / 9

So, x = 15; y = 9

Put the value of x and y saving of Aswath, Sunita and Ramdin.

=> 12x -15y : 9x - 9y : 7x - 8y

=> (12 × 15 - 15 × 9) : (9 × 15 – 9 × 9) : (7 × 15 - 8 × 9)

=> (180 - 135) : (135 - 81) : (105 - 72)

=> 45 : 54 : 33

Divided by 3,

=> 15 : 18 : 11

Hence, ‘15 : 18 : 11’ is the ratio of the savings of Aswath, Sunita and Ramdin.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the equation.

512 * 32 * 9 * 100 * 6 * 25 * 2
questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule

Given equation 512 * 32 * 9 * 100 * 6 * 25 * 2

Option 1 : Using the combination +, ×, ÷, =, -, ×

512 + 32 × 9 ÷ 100 = 6 - 25 × 2

By BODMAS rule

512 + 32 × 0.09 = 6 - 25 × 2

512 + 2.88 = 6 - 50

514.88 = - 44 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : Using combination ÷, ×, +, -, =, ×

512 ÷ 32 × 9 + 100 - 6 = 25 × 2

16 × 9 + 100 - 6 = 25 × 2

144 + 100 - 6 = 50

244 – 6 = 50

238 = 50 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3 : Using the combination ÷, ×, +, =, -, ×

512 ÷ 32 × 9 + 100 = 6 - 25 × 2

16 × 9 + 100 = 6 - 25 × 2

144 + 100 = 6 - 50

244 = - 44 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4 : Using the combination ÷, ×, -, +, =, ×

512 ÷ 32 × 9 - 100 + 6 = 25 × 2

16 × 9 - 100 + 6 = 25 × 2

144 - 100 + 6 = 50

44 + 6 = 50

50 = 50 (LHS = RHS)

Hence, the answer is “÷, ×, -, +, =, ×”.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the first rocket launched in India?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years was the first rocket launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1963.

Key Points

  • The first rocket launched in India:
    • Sounding rockets are one or two-stage solid propellant rockets used for probing the upper atmospheric regions and for space research.
    • They also serve as easily affordable platforms to test or prove prototypes of new components or subsystems intended for use in launch vehicles and satellites.
    • With the establishment of the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) in 1963 at Thumba, a location close to the magnetic equator, there was a quantum jump in the scope for aeronomy and atmospheric sciences in India.
    • The launch of the first sounding rocket from Thumba near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala on 21 November 1963, marked the beginning of the Indian Space Programme. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
    • Sounding rockets made it possible to probe the atmosphere in situ using rocket-borne instrumentation.
    • The first rockets were two-stage rockets imported from Russia (M-100) and France (Centaure).
    • While the M-100 could carry a payload of 70 kg to an altitude of 85 km, the Centaure was capable of reaching 150 km with a payload of approximately 30 kg.

Additional Information

  • ISRO:
    • It is the space agency under the Department of Space of Government of India, headquartered in the city of Bengaluru, Karnataka.
    • Its vision is to harness space technology for national development while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration.
    • Antrix Corporation Limited (ACL) is a Marketing arm of ISRO for promotion and commercial exploitation of space products, technical consultancy services, and transfer of technologies developed by ISRO.
    • The space research activities were initiated in India under Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the founding father of the Indian space programme, during the 1960s.

    • The national park is characterized by many floating decomposed plant materials locally called phumdis.
    • The park which was initially declared to be a sanctuary in 1966, was subsequently declared to be a national park in 1977 through a gazette notification.
    • Kishtwar National Park is a national park located in the Kishtwar district of Jammu and Kashmir, India.
    • Khangchendzonga National Park also Kanchenjunga Biosphere Reserve is a National Park and a Biosphere reserve located in Sikkim, India.

    • Jim Corbett National Park is a forested wildlife sanctuary in northern India’s Uttarakhand State.

Additional Information

questions.question: Which of the following gases is naturally formed via the anaerobic decay of phosphorus containing organic matter?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following gases is naturally formed via the anaerobic decay of phosphorus containing organic matter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Phosphine.

Key Points

  • Phosphine:
    • It is the simplest phosphorus hydride.
    • It is a colourless and extremely toxic gas.
    • Some people think it smells like rotting fish; it reminds others of the odour of garlic.
    • In any case, pure phosphine is actually odourless; an impurity, diphosphine (P2H4), is responsible for its foul scent.
    • It is formed naturally via the anaerobic decay of phosphorus-containing organic matter. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
    • The earliest reported preparation was made by Antoine Lavoisier’s student Philippe Gengembre in the late 18th century.
    • It is made industrially from white phosphorus by hydrolysis with an alkali metal hydroxide or an aqueous acid-catalyzed disproportionation reaction.
    • The industrial product is normally shipped as liquefied gas.

Hence the phosphine is formed naturally via anaerobic decay of phosphorus-containing organic matter.

    • The 16th group is known as Chalcogen.
    • The 15th group is known as Pnictogen.
  • The s-block elements include alkali metals and alkaline earth metals. 
  • The d-block elements include Transition elements.
  • The f-block elements include Inner Transition Elements.

questions.question: Terrace farming is done on which of the following types of land?
questions.questionHtml: Terrace farming is done on which of the following types of land?
questions.solution: Terrace farming is practiced on hilly or sloped lands to prevent soil erosion and manage water efficiently. This technique is particularly effective in areas with uneven terrains, where traditional farming methods are not suitable due to the risk of soil degradation and water wastage.

questions.question: Which phenomenon deals with the scattering of light by molecules of a medium when they are excited to vibrational energy levels?
questions.questionHtml: Which phenomenon deals with the scattering of light by molecules of a medium when they are excited to vibrational energy levels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Raman Effect.

Key Point

  • Raman Effect:
    • It states that there is a change in the wavelength of light that occurs when a light beam is deflected by molecules.  
    • This is caused due to the molecules of gases, liquids, or solids when they are excited to vibrational energy levels. 
    • The Raman Effect is the phenomenon of scattering of light by molecules present in a medium.​ Hence, Option 3 is correct.
    • When a beam of light travels through a transparent object, a small fraction of the light gets scattered in directions other than where it should.
    • The scattering occurs due to the difference in wavelength of light as it enters into the medium.
    • The Raman effect is defined as the scattering of photons by the excited molecules that are at higher energy levels.
    • Raman effect is also known as Raman scattering.
    • Raman effect, change in the wavelength of light that occurs when a light beam is deflected by molecules.
    • When a beam of light traverses a dust-free, transparent sample of a chemical compound, a small fraction of the light emerges in directions other than that of the incident (incoming) beam.
    • Most of this scattered light is of unchanged wavelength.
    • A small part, however, has wavelengths different from that of the incident light its presence is a result of the Raman effect.

questions.questionHtml: What is the difference between the compound interest (in Rs.) compounded yearly and compounded half yearly for 18 months at 20% per annum on a sum of Rs. 12,000?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal amount = Rs. 12000

Time = 18 months

Rate of interest = 20%

Concept used:

Simple interest = (Principal × Time × Rate) ÷ 100

In the case of compound interest,

A = P × (1 + r/100)n

C.I = A - P

Here, A = Amount, P = Principal, r = Rate of interest. n = Time, C.I = Compound interest

Calculation:

When interest is compounded yearly,

Principal = Rs. 12,000

At the end of the first year, the principal becomes = 12000 × 1.21 = Rs. 14400

Then, after 6 months the interest accumulated on the principal amount of Rs. 14400

⇒ (14400 × 20 × 6/12) / 100

⇒ 1440

So, after 8 months the initial principal amount becomes = 14400 + 1440 = Rs. 15840

Interest accumuted in 18 months = Rs. (15840 - 12000) = Rs. 3840

When interest compounded half-yearly,

Rate of interest (R) = 20/2 % = 10%

Time (n) = 18 ÷ 6 = 3

Principal = 12,000

So, after 18 months the principal becomes

⇒ 12000 (1 + 10/100)3

⇒ Rs. 15972

Interest accumuted in 18 months = Rs. (15972 - 12000) = Rs. 3972

So, the difference between the interest accumulated = Rs. (3972 - 3840) = Rs. 132

∴ The difference between the compound interest compounded yearly and compounded half yearly for 18 months at 20% per annum on a sum of Rs. 12,000 is Rs. 132.

CIhalf yearly – CIyearly = 12000 [(1 + (1/10))3– (1 + (1/5))1.5]

CIhalf yearly – CIyearly = 132

⇒ (x3- x-3) = 8 + 6

⇒ (x3- x-3) = 14

questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, points A, B, C and D in this order are concyclic such that BD is a diameter of the circle. If ∠BAC = 22°, then find the measure (in degrees) of ∠COD.
questions.solution:
Given:

Centre O

The points A, B, C, and D in this order are concyclic.

BD is the diameter

∠BAC = 22°

Concept used:

The angle formed on circumference forming on diameter is 90° 

The angle at the center formed on the same arc is twice the angle on the same arc forming at the circumference. 

Calculation:

Here, according to the concept, 

∠ BAD = 90°

⇒ ∠ BAC + ∠ CAD = 90° 

⇒ ∠ CAD = 90° - 22° = 68° 

Now we know that, 

∠ COD = 2 × ∠ CAD 

⇒ ∠ COD = 2 × 68 = 136°   

∴ The measure of ∠COD is 136°.

questions.question: By mistake, the reciprocal of a positive fraction got typed in place of itself, and thereby its value got reduced by \(\frac{175}{4}\%\) . What was the value of the fraction?

The reciprocal of a positive fraction got typed in place of itself, and thereby its value got reduced to \(\frac{175}{4}\%\).

Application of percentage

According to the question,

 \(x - \frac{1}{x}=\frac{175x}{400}\)

Cross multiplying

400(x2 - 1) = 175x2

400x2 - 175x2 = 400

⇒ (x)2 = 400/225

⇒ (x) = 20/15 (∵ the fraction should be positive)

⇒ (x) = 4/3

questions.question: Triangle ABC is right angled at B. BD is an altitude intersecting AC at D. If AC = 9 cm and CD = 3 cm. then find the measure of AB (in cm).
questions.questionHtml: Triangle ABC is right angled at B. BD is an altitude intersecting AC at D. If AC = 9 cm and CD = 3 cm. then find the measure of AB (in cm).
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC is a right-angled triangle at B.

BD⊥AC

AC = 9 cm

CD = 3 cm

Concept used:

If ΔABC is right-angled triangle at B and BD⊥AC, then

ΔABC ~ ΔBDC ~ ΔADB and

AB2 = AD × AC

BC2 = DC × AC

BD2 = AD × DC

If ΔABC is a right-angled triangle at B & AC is the hypotenuse, then according to Pythagoras theorem,

AB2 + BC2 = AC2

Calculation:

Taking two similar triangle ΔABC & ΔBDC,

BC2 = DC × AC

⇒ BC2 = CD × AC

⇒ BC2 = 3 × 9

⇒ BC2 = 27

From ΔABC,

AB2 + BC2 = AC2

⇒ AB2 = AC2 - BC2

⇒ AB2 = 92 - 27

⇒ AB2 = 54

⇒ AB = 3√6

∴ The measure of AB is 3√6 cm.

questions.question: What is the average of numbers from 1 to 50 which are multiples of 2 or 5? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.questionHtml: What is the average of numbers from 1 to 50 which are multiples of 2 or 5? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Given:

Number range = 1 to 50

Numbers should be multiples of 2 or 5.

Concept used:

Average = (1st term + last term)/2

Average = Sum of elements/No. of elements

Total number of terms = tn= a + d(n − 1)

n = number of terms

a = 1st term

d = commons difference

Calculation:

For 2

Number of terms → 50 = 2 + 2n - 2

⇒ n = 25

Average = (2 + 50)/2 = 26

Total = 26 × 25 = 650

For 5

Number of terms → 50 = 5 + 5n - 5

⇒ n = 10

Average = (5 + 50)/2 = 27.5

Total = 27.5 × 10 = 275

10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 come two times

So,

Effective total = 650 + 275 - 150

⇒ 775

Now, the number of terms that are multiples of 2 or 5 = 25 + 10 - 5 = 30

Average = 775 ÷ 30 ≈ 25.8

∴ The average of the numbers from 1 to 50 which are multiples of 2 or 5 is 25.8.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. At its height, around 1,200 years ago, the city of Calakmul had a population of about 50,000 people, but the kingdom as a whole numbered more than 1.5 million.

B. Deep in the jungle of southern Mexico lie the ruins of a city that thrived for centuries before it was abandoned more than 1,000 years ago.

D. Calakmul was once one of the two duelling superpowers-along with Tikal-of the Classical Mayan civilisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BDAC'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
  • Sentence B will be the first sentence because it is an independent general statement. It is talking about a city located in the jungle of southern Mexico that was abandoned more than 1000 years ago.
  • Sentence D will be the next sentence because it further explains Sentence B. It tells us that the abandoned city was named Calakmul.
  • Sentence A will be the next sentence because it tells about the details of Calakmul city, its population, etc.
  • At last, sentence C will be used.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is:
    • B: Deep in the jungle of southern Mexico lie the ruins of a city that thrived for centuries before it was abandoned more than 1,000 years ago.
    • D: Calakmul was once one of the two duelling superpowers-along with Tikal-of the Classical Mayan civilisation.

    • C: Archaeologists have uncovered 6,750 structures here-the largest is this pyramid temple, called, simply, 'Structure 2.'
       

Correct Sequence: Deep in the jungle of southern Mexico lie the ruins of a city that thrived for centuries before it was abandoned more than 1,000 years ago. Calakmul was once one of the two duelling superpowers-along with Tikal-of the Classical Mayan civilisation. At its height, around 1,200 years ago, the city of Calakmul had a population of about 50,000 people, but the kingdom as a whole numbered more than 1.5 million. Archaeologists have uncovered 6,750 structures here-the largest is this pyramid temple, called, simply, 'Structure 2.'

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. “I have already spent it,” the thief replied.

B. “What! I will take you to the police right now,” Arun thundered.

C. “Give me back my money,” Arun said to the thief.

D. “Sir, please have some mercy on me,” the thief pleaded.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CABD'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
  • Sentence C will be the first sentence because it is the starting of an incident. It is talking about Arun threatening the thief so that he gives his money back.
  • Sentence A will be the next sentence because it further explains what that thief did with the money.
  • Sentence B will be the next sentence because it tells what Arun reciprocated after he listened to the thief spending his money.
  • Lastly, Sentence D will be used.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is:
    • C: “Give me back my money,” Arun said to the thief.
    • A: “I have already spent it,” the thief replied.
    • B: “What! I will take you to the police right now,” Arun thundered.
    • D: “Sir, please have some mercy on me,” the thief pleaded.
       

Correct Sequence: “Give me back my money,” Arun said to the thief. “I have already spent it,” the thief replied. “What! I will take you to the police right now,” Arun thundered. “Sir, please have some mercy on me,” the thief pleaded.
